title: Early-acceptance signal and fallback controller for kernel-aware speculative decode
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight early-acceptance signal and centralized fallback controller that integrates kernel-aware telemetry to make per-request speculative decode routing decisions. The feature should reduce wasted decode work on slower kernels or model variants while preserving tail-latency SLOs and minimizing quality regressions.

Scope:
- Define an early-acceptance signal emitted during prefill (or first decode tokens) that represents a model variant's likelihood of producing an accepted continuation.
- Build a fallback controller that aggregates acceptance signals plus kernel execution characteristics (latency distribution, GPU occupancy hints, quantization profile) to decide immediate fallback or continue.
- Wire signal telemetry into Console traces and per-route cost/latency breakdowns for visibility and alerting.
- Provide a conservative A/B rollout path and telemetry gating to revert if quality or latency regressions appear.

Non-goals: Full probabilistic re-ranking of candidates, re-training models to optimize signal, or deep kernel scheduling changes (those are future follow-ups).
comments: 2025-02-13 Priya: Drafted acceptance signal schema — lightweight integer score (0-100) plus reason tag. Kept payload small to avoid decode hot path overhead.

2025-02-18 Marcus: Ran microbenchmarks with 10k synthetic short prompts. Observed that some kernels (int8 quantized) show 20-40% longer prefill latency variance on long-seq requests. Acceptance signal helps avoid spending decode on slower candidates.
2025-02-22 Review (PM): Sarah Chen requested a hard safety cutoff to never fallback for whitelisted enterprise routes. Added route-level opt-outs.
2025-02-24 Design feedback: Elena (Design) asked for clear Console visualization for 'acceptance drift' over time. Added event types for drift and transient spike detection.
2025-02-27 Marcus: Prototype integrated with runtime; added a simulated fallback policy using simple threshold + kernel-latency multiplier. Numeric thresholds tuned on internal log replay dataset.

2025-02-28 QA: Short smoke test passes on dedicated GPUs. Observed one regression: for prompts with heavy prefix overlap, acceptance signal sometimes underestimates and triggers fallback unnecessarily. Added cache-warmup exception clause.
2025-03-01 Priya: Planning canary rollout: 2% traffic on hosted, route-scoped experiment, monitor acceptance_rate, decoding_cpu_ms, tail P95 latency, and hallucination_rate on eval prompt set.
decisions: Use a compact integer acceptance_score (0-100) instead of full confidence vector to minimize RPC payload and CPU overhead.
Make fallback decisions deterministic on controller side: acceptance_score < threshold OR estimated_kernel_latency > route_latency_budget * multiplier triggers fallback.
Kernel-aware multipliers will be configurable by kernel family (e.g., int8-onnx, bf16-cuda) to reflect observed variance instead of hard-coding per-model values.
Route-level opt-out required for enterprise SLAs; default behavior enabled for public hosted routes.
Telemetry events emitted: acceptance_emit, fallback_decision, fallback_execute, acceptance_drift_alert.
tradeoffs: Compact signal reduces accuracy vs fuller probabilities but preserves critical path performance.
Controller-based fallback centralizes logic but adds a small decision latency; we mitigate this by co-locating controller with serving shard and caching kernel multipliers.
Conservative thresholds reduce false fallbacks but may miss cost savings; aggressive thresholds save cost but risk quality regressions. Hence we will A/B test.
perf_targets: No more than 1% increase in median decode path CPU time for emitting the acceptance signal.
Fallback controller decision latency < 300us p95 when co-located with runtime shard.
10-20% reduction in wasted decode token-count for routes with multi-variant speculative routing in our replay dataset.
observability: Instrument acceptance_score histogram and per-kernel latency distributions.
Add Console widgets: route-level acceptance_rate, fallback_rate, post-fallback quality delta (using eval prompt set), and cost_saved_estimate.
Add alerts: fallback_rate > 5% sustained for 15m, acceptance_drift_alert when acceptance_score mean drops > 10 points on important routes.
next_steps: Complete integration tests for KV-cache warmup exception and route opt-outs (owner: Marcus, 3d).
